summary:
NCR carries the strongest protective legal framework in the Philippines: Quezon City enacted SP-3417, S-2025, a comprehensive SOGIESC anti-discrimination ordinance, and in July 2025 became the first LGU in the country to enact a Gender-Inclusive Health Ordinance creating a framework for gender-affirming primary care and specialised services. For a visitor, these represent the only enforceable protections in a country with no national anti-discrimination statute covering gender identity—complaint routes to a city health office or the QC Gender Desk that simply do not exist elsewhere.

Against that, two of the six documented killings of trans women in the 2024–2025 national series occurred here (Shaina Bayabay strangled in Pasig, March 2024; "Christine" stabbed in Valenzuela, September 2025), and EARIST state college reportedly denied enrollment to trans women requiring short haircuts (March 2024 video). The Commission on Human Rights issued public statements condemning both the campus practice and the killings, and arrests followed in Valenzuela.

Net effect: +0.09 above the national score. The ordinance belt gives a discovered visitor tangible institutional recourse unavailable in sibling regions; the violence, while real, is matched by arrests and official condemnation rather than impunity. Compare Soccsksargen (0.44), where a targeted activist assassination drew the CHR's own "cruelty and impunity" language without comparable protective infrastructure.

sources.summary: Quezon City public notice: ordinance SP-3417, S-2025, 'providing for a comprehensive anti-discrimination policy on the basis of sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics (SOGIESC)', revising the city's 2014 Gender-Fair Ordinance (SP-2357, S-2014); posted as a 22nd City Council ordinance with the full text downloadable.

Quezon City government press release: the city became the first local government unit in the Philippines to enact a comprehensive Gender-Inclusive Health Ordinance (July 2025), introduced by councilors Bernard Herrera and Dorothy Delarmente, creating a framework for gender-affirming primary care, mental-health support and specialised medical services through the city public-health system; quoted from Mayor Joy Belmonte.

Transrespectful/trans murder documentation site (TDoR2 memorial) report entry: Shaina Bayabay, 29, Pasig City, Metro Manila, Philippines - 1 March 2024, category violence, cause strangled; the underlying report adds that she was killed during a drinking session.

TDoR2 memorial report entry: 'Christine', 44, Valenzuela City, Metro Manila, Philippines - 22 September 2025, category violence, cause stabbed; the underlying report adds she was a college-educated therapist found in a rented apartment after neighbours heard an argument, and two men were arrested.

Official Commission on Human Rights (Philippines) statement over the viral video of a transgender woman compelled to get a haircut as a condition for enrollment at the Eulogio 'Amang' Rodriguez Institute of Science and Technology (EARIST) in Manila: the CHR expresses deep concern, notes the 2021 student handbook requires male students to get a barber's haircut while complaints continue despite repeated joint discussions and demand letters from groups including Bahagari-EARIST, and urges an impartial investigation and a review of the code of conduct in the context of exercising SOGIE.

localsOnly: The Gender-Inclusive Health Ordinance's clinical services - gender-affirming primary care and mental-health support in city facilities - are what residents use; what a visitor can actually invoke is the anti-discrimination complaint machinery (the QC Gender Desk and city health office routes).
